title: Settings at 800px cuts the user's name to 'A.'
where: Settings, right-hand detail pane: Profile card and Sign-in rows
why: At 800px the page keeps three columns (app sidebar, settings nav, detail), which leaves the detail pane about 260px wide. The profile card shows 'A.' and '@.' instead of 'Ada Audit' and '@audit_ada', and the Sign-in rows cut off as 'Email & rec...' and 'audit_ada@au...'. The user cannot read their own account details. Below about 1000px the settings nav or the app sidebar should collapse.

title: Project Hub says 'Nothing more to vote on' while a Book Club vote is waiting
where: Book Club Hub, first line of the FOR YOU card
why: Other screens agree the user owes a vote: Communities shows '1 vote waiting on you · Book Club', the bot's NEEDS YOU lists Book Club with a Vote link, and the request page shows 'Needs 2 more yes' with a Vote button. The project's own Hub says 'Nothing more to vote on.' The Hub is the project's front door, and here it hides the one decision the user owes.

title: In-progress and needs-you counts disagree between screens
where: Homeroom bot list header compared with the Hub's 'Your work' row and the Communities Book Club row
why: The bot header reads 'Needs you: 1 · In progress: 0', while the Hub ('Your work · 1 in progress') and Communities ('1 in progress · 2 new messages') both count one item in progress. The header also uses 'Label: number' and shows a zero. House style is counts as words, with zero showing nothing.

title: Thread status rows break open the bot's chat bubbles
where: Homeroom bot, Main Chat column: the 9:24 PM 'Plan:' bubble and the 9:28 PM 'Your change to Book Club is ready to try' bubble
why: The 9:24 bubble has no bottom edge and the 9:28 bubble has no top edge. The 'B ▷ #1 Let members suggest... Ready for your yes · 4 updates' row sits across the gap, so the two messages look like one broken frame with a row painted over it. This looks like a rendering glitch at every width.

title: Homeroom bot at 800px squeezes three columns side by side
where: Homeroom bot: list column header, community chips, Needs you row and the approval card in chat
why: The title 'Homeroom bot' wraps onto two lines next to the + button. 'Needs you: 1 · / In progress: 0' also wraps. The community chips are cut off mid-chip (only the 'W' of Watering Rota shows), and the Needs you row cuts off as 'Let members su...'. In the chat, the approval card puts Try it, Approve, Change something and Withdraw it in a vertical stack beside a text column about 200px wide. At this width, show the list or the chat, not both next to the expanded sidebar.

title: Discover at 800px: two-column grid cuts off every card subtitle
where: Discover, ALL APPS grid
why: Each card is about 250px wide. Titles wrap onto two lines ('Group / challenge', 'Find a / time'), every subtitle cuts off as 'Updated 2...', and the Homeroom card's description shows only 'The commu...'. The same cards fit on one line at 1024. A single column would fit at this width.

title: Discover: card grid runs edge to edge while search and tabs stay narrow on the left
where: Discover from 1280px up: search field, For you/Browse/Joined control, ALL APPS label and grid
why: The search field and segmented control stop at about 580px and stay pinned left, while the three-column grid stretches to the right edge. At 1920 each card is about 540px wide, with the Join button far from the title. The 'ALL APPS' label and the 'Demos and apps needing fixes...' note are indented relative to the card edges, and there is about 100px of empty space between Filters and the label. The 'For you' tab is also headed 'ALL APPS'.

title: Each top-level screen uses a different content width and alignment
where: Main column on Home, Discover, Communities, Messages, Profile, Hub and Challenges
why: At 1920 the main column is centred at about 1000px on Home, Profile and Settings, 640px on Communities, 690px on Messages, 760px on Hub and the request page, and about 1640px edge to edge on Discover and in conversations. Challenges pins its tabs left and centres its message. Moving between sidebar items makes the content jump in width and position.

title: Messages never shows the list and a conversation side by side
where: Messages list and conversation views from 1280px up
why: The list is a single column of about 700px floating in a full-width sheet, with the rest of the screen empty. Opening a chat replaces the list, so switching chats always means going back. The Homeroom bot tab already shows a list and a chat together at these widths; Messages should do the same.

title: Conversations stretch across the whole window
where: Direct message and group chat threads at 1440 and 1920
why: At 1920 the thread is about 1650px wide. Received bubbles sit at the far left and sent bubbles at the far right, about 1500px apart, and the composer spans the full width. It is hard to follow who said what. Cap the thread width as the request page does (about 760px).

title: Group chat 'Flat 4B' is filed under 'Direct messages'
where: Messages list section label and the sidebar sub-heading under Messages
why: Flat 4B has 3 members ('you own this group') but appears under DIRECT MESSAGES in the list and under 'Direct messages' in the sidebar. Its avatar is also drawn three ways: a stacked pair in the list, a single 'A' tile in the sidebar and a single 'A' circle in the chat header.

title: Sender names are formatted differently in DMs and groups, and your name repeats on every message
where: Name and time line above each message bubble
why: Group chats put '@' before every sender (@audit_cy, @audit_ada), but the DM shows 'audit_ben' without it. Your own name and time repeat in blue above every one of your bubbles, even consecutive ones sent in the same minute. That uses the action accent on a label and adds noise.

title: Project top bar changes colour and controls between the App and Hub tabs
where: Top bar on Book Club's App tab compared with its Hub and request pages
why: On the App tab the bar is light, with a periwinkle 'Suggest' pill. On the Hub and request pages the same project's bar turns solid teal and Suggest disappears. On the Hub, the primary 'Open app' button is also teal instead of the single blue action accent. The same project looks like two different products.

title: Sidebar count badges change colour and shape, or vanish, depending on the page
where: Left sidebar, Communities list
why: Book Club's blue '1' disappears when its row expands, and its 'Needs you' sub-row shows no count. 'All 4 communities' shows a blue '1' on most pages but a grey one on the Hub. Homeroom bot shows a grey '1' circle at 800. #general has a grey '2 unread' pill, while the Hub shows the same messages as a blue '2 new' pill. One kind of count gets four different treatments, and the one that matters disappears when you open the project.

title: Unexplained grey dot on the project's App row
where: Left sidebar, the highlighted 'App' sub-row under each project
why: Every project's highlighted App row has a grey dot at its right edge, with no label or tooltip. House style keeps status dots for when something is wrong, so a dot with no meaning reads as a warning.

title: Workshop and Proposals shots both show the Hub
where: Book Club project page
why: At every width, the Workshop shots and the Proposals shots both show Book Club's Hub, with 'Hub' highlighted in the sidebar, and the two are identical. The Workshop board and the proposals list never appear. Either those routes redirect to the Hub or they cannot be reached directly. Worth checking which.

title: Audience and container names vary from screen to screen
where: Communities filter chips, Hub subtitle, Home and Discover headings
why: The filter chips read 'Public 2 · Private 1 · Just you 1', and the Hub calls Book Club a 'Private community', but the product's audience names are Just you, Group and Community. Home lists the same things as 'My apps' and 'Discover Communities', Discover says 'ALL APPS', and Communities offers 'Make a project'. Across screens, users see app, project, community, group, private and public for overlapping ideas.

title: Section headings use three different styles
where: Labels above card groups on Home compared with Discover, Communities, Profile and Hub
why: Home puts large bold sentence-case headings over its cards ('My apps', 'Challenges') plus one in Title Case ('Discover Communities'). Discover, Communities, Profile and Hub use small bold uppercase labels ('ALL APPS', 'NEEDS YOU', 'YOUR WORK'). House style is the small uppercase label.

title: Home: My apps icons are spread across the full width
where: Home, My apps row
why: Four icons about 56px wide are justified across the whole column with gaps of about 190px, so the row looks scattered rather than like a grid. At 800, 'Neighbourhood Swap' wraps even though the row has space to spare. A left-aligned grid with fixed spacing would hold together.

title: Home search field sits right against the top bar
where: Home, top of the main column
why: The 'Search your apps...' field starts directly under the top bar with almost no gap (about 3px at 1920), so it looks clipped by the bar. Discover and Communities leave about 24px above their search fields.

title: Discover Communities carousel cuts off the last card and its Join button
where: Home, Discover Communities row, right edge
why: The last visible card fades out cut mid-word ('Lend... Updat... 1 cont...'), and at 800 its Join pill shows only '+ J'. With no arrows or scroll hint on desktop, the row looks broken rather than scrollable.

title: Request page: scrolled text shows through, sliced, under the sticky title
where: Request #1, just below the sticky REQUEST #1 header
why: When the body scrolls, its lines are cut horizontally under the sticky header. At 1920 a second copy of the title 'Let members suggest a book and vote on the next one' appears sliced in half right below the real one. At 1440 a line of the description is cut through the middle. At 800 only a stray grey bar from the quote border is left. The header needs an opaque background with a divider or fade.

title: Request: the same vote appears three ways, in four colours
where: Request page: Votes card, change header and the bot message's chips
why: The Votes card shows 'Needs 2 more yes' and a blue Vote button. At 1920 the change header adds a purple 'Vote · 0/2' pill. The bot's message then adds four outlined chips in purple, blue, green and red: '0 of 2 yes votes', 'Preview', 'Yes (0)' and 'No (0)'. These show zero counts, use colours outside the single-accent palette and put four pills in one row.

title: Request thread copy: '1 reply' above five entries, and 'created issue'
where: Request page: thread divider and timeline
why: The divider says '1 reply' but five entries follow. The first event reads 'audit_ada created issue' although the product calls these requests. The request title ('...a book and vote on the next one') and the plan and change title ('...books and vote on the next read') differ, and the change is numbered '#3' on request '#1'. It is hard to tell which thing is which.

title: Request page: no highlighted sidebar row, active send button on an empty box, timestamps on their own line
where: Request page: sidebar, reply composer and timeline
why: None of App, Hub, Needs you or Workshop is highlighted, so the sidebar loses its 'you are here'. The empty 'Reply...' box shows a solid blue send button, while every other composer greys it out until there is text. At 1024 to 1440, '· 9:24 PM' wraps onto a line of its own under the plan entry.

title: Profile shows large '0 live' and '0 challenges' tiles
where: Profile, the two stat tiles under the profile card
why: Two large cards show only zeros, against the rule that zero shows nothing. '0 live' also contradicts the Hub ('Book Club · Live since today') and the bot ('LIVE THIS WEEK · 1'), so the number looks wrong.

title: Profile's two-column layout squeezes the left column
where: Profile from 1024px up
why: The left column is about 350px wide and the right about 610px. In the left column, '@audit_ada · Building / since November 2026' wraps and 'What you are told about, here and i...' cuts off, while the right column has room. The section order also changes from 800, where Your work comes first. The SETTINGS group repeats the 'Edit profile' button (Profile row) and the sidebar gear (Settings row).

title: Settings nav cuts off its own labels on wide screens
where: Settings, left nav column
why: From 1280px up, 'Linked phones' becomes 'Linked ph... 1 linked', and 'INTEGRATIONS & AUTOMATION' wraps onto two lines at every width. The nav is fixed at about 225px while hundreds of pixels sit empty either side.

title: Settings: 'Account' is selected but the page opens on 'Profile', under three large headings
where: Settings detail pane and search field
why: The highlighted nav item is 'Account', but the pane opens on 'Profile', followed by 'Sign-in' and 'Delete account', all the same large size. House style allows one large heading per page. The 'Find a setting' field is also grey-filled with no search icon, unlike every other search field in the shell.

title: Challenges empty state is a bare line, misaligned with its tabs
where: Challenges / Standings page
why: The empty state is one grey sentence centred across the page, while the Challenges/Standings control is pinned left. On Home the same empty state is a card with a title and a hint ('No challenges right now / New ones will show up here.'). At 1920 the control sits at the left with nothing beneath it.

title: Content panes ride up into the top bar
where: Top edge of the Homeroom bot chat pane and the Messages and conversation sheets
why: The right-hand chat pane and the Messages sheet start a few pixels above the top bar's bottom edge, so their rounded corners overlap the bar. This is clearest at 800 and 1024. The Messages sheets also stack a second rounded panel behind the conversation card, with right edges that do not line up.

title: Bot list rows: a gap after '#1', and several pills per thread row
where: Homeroom bot: NEEDS YOU and LIVE THIS WEEK rows, and thread rows in Main Chat
why: In the list rows, '#1' sits in its own column about 70px before the title, leaving a hole. Thread rows in the chat stack a community avatar, a status tile, a green '#1' pill and a 'Live' label. House style is at most one pill per row.

title: Hub repeats the project name, and Recently live is mostly empty
where: Book Club Hub
why: 'Book Club' appears in the top bar, again as a large hero heading under a separate large 'Hub' heading, and a third time as the only Recently live card. That card's teal tile fills about a third of a full-width panel, and the rest of the panel is empty.

title: Just-you project shows a channel and a bare time
where: Communities list row for Watering Rota; sidebar under Watering Rota
why: Watering Rota's row has only '16m ago' as its subtitle, with no verb and no context, while the other rows give member counts. Opening this one-person project still lists 'Channels › # general' in the sidebar, a chat channel nobody else can post in.
